extracted.intended_audience: prospective patent applicants, patent agents, and filers (domestic and foreign) using CNIPA procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Practical procedural guidance and formal requirements for filing, examination, publication, payment, PCT national-phase and registration of patents and IC layout-designs with the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA).

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted submission channels for patent applications: E-filing, Mailing, Hand-delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E-filing is available via CNIPA electronic filing websites/clients; mailing and hand-delivery are also accepted. (See registration/e-filing instructions elsewhere in the guidance.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Elements required by patent type
rubrics_metrics.description: Required documents vary by patent type: Invention — request, claim(s) and description; Utility model — request, claim(s), description and drawing(s); Design — request, drawing(s) or photograph(s) and brief description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must include the specified elements for the declared patent type at filing to avoid formal defects or non-acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances of non-acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances that will cause the application not to be accepted include: not in Chinese; handwritten, vague, altered, or easily erased submissions; mailed directly from somewhere outside Mainland China; unclear patent type; divisional application changing the type of patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submission language, legibility, origin of mailing, and clear identification of patent type to avoid non-acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of electronic filing users — identity documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity requirements for registering on the China Patent Electronic Filing Website: Individuals provide identity number; entities provide unified social credit number; patent agencies provide patent agency registration number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the required identity numbers to obtain a formal electronic filing user account. If other valid identity documents are submitted, only a temporary account will be created and further mailing of documents to CNIPA will be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic registration outcomes and completion steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful registration yields registration result, user ID and password indicated on the receipt automatically; a new formal user is created and no paper approval notice will be issued. If only temporary account is created, relevant documents must be mailed to CNIPA to finish formal registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mailing address for completing registration is provided (Receiving Division, CNIPA, No.6 Xitucheng Road, Haidian District, Beijing, 100088).

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment channels and date of payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple payment modes are accepted: Bank transfer (CNIPA bank account), post office remittance, on-site handling (cash, check, debit/credit card, WeChat Pay, Alipay), and online payment via fee management system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on which the transfer is conducted shall be the date of payment; the date of remittance issued by the post office shall be the date of payment; the payment date is the day CNIPA gets complete payment information. Ensure application number (or patent number) and the name of fees are indicated correctly when paying. Use http://fee.cnipa.gov.cn for online payment management and inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examination scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary examination for invention applications includes: formal examination of application documents and other documents; examination on obvious substantive defects; checking of fees; and checking of time limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary examination determines whether the application proceeds to publication/substantive examination or triggers notifications to correct formalities or office actions for substantive defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications to correct / office actions and consequences of non-response
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving a Notification to Correct Formalities or a Notification to Make Correction/Office Action, the applicant must submit the correction request and corrected documents or submit corrections/observations with corrected documents within the time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no response is made within the time limit, the request is deemed not to be submitted and the application is deemed withdrawn. If defects are not overcome the application is rejected; if defects are overcome, the request is approved and the application passes preliminary examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative reconsideration (appealable administrative actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant is not satisfied with a specific administrative action of CNIPA (except rejection), the applicant may request administrative reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection is excluded from this remedy (different procedures such as reexamination may apply).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international-phase applicability and filing methods
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT procedures apply to invention or utility model applications; international filing languages include Chinese or English; filing methods include E-filing (CEPCT Website or Client Tool), Hand delivery, Mailing and Fax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International filing date = date of receipt of an international application complying with prescribed requirements. There is a 1-month time limit (specified) for certain submissions from filing date — follow CNIPA/PCT guidance for exact deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT timeline milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical PCT milestones shown: transmittal of International Search Report (ISR) and written opinion, international publication (generally around 18 months from priority), optional supplementary international search and demand for international preliminary examination, transmittal of SISR or IPRP II, and PCT national-phase entry (commonly 30 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should track the PCT timeline (priority/filing date) to meet deadlines for supplementary search, demand, and national-phase entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT international-phase fees and reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees for the international phase: search fee (CNY 2100), international filing fee (CHF 1330), additional fee (CHF 15 per sheet), priority document fee (CNY 150/doc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reductions: E-filing discounts (PDF -200 CHF / XML -300 CHF); Chinese individual applicants get a 90% reduction in international filing fee and additional fees. Modes of payment include online payment, counter payment, bank transfer, and authorization to charge a current account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of PCT application in China — requirements and loss of effect
rubrics_metrics.description: An international application will have effect in China only if: it conforms with PCT Article 11, is accorded a filing date, and designates China.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loss of effect (i.e., application ineffective in China) occurs when: no designation of China; the international application has been withdrawn or deemed withdrawn or designation of China withdrawn; no request for entering the national phase within the time limit; or failure to meet minimum requirements for entering the national phase even after 32 months from the priority date. If the PCT application has no effect in China or effect is lost, it cannot enter the China national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for earlier publication of invention application
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request earlier publication by checking 'please publish as soon as possible' in the request or by submitting an unconditional request for earlier publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation of publication starts promptly after passing preliminary examination. Once the request for earlier publication is approved and the publication preparation has started, the request cannot be withdrawn; the publication process proceeds regardless of any withdrawal or suspension of the patent application. Patent applications passing preliminary examination are published promptly after the expiration of 18 months from the filing date (or priority date where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of patent right — formalities, fees and time limit to complete registration
rubrics_metrics.description: After grant, CNIPA issues the Notification to grant patent right and Notification to go through formalities of registration. The applicant must go through registration formalities and pay related fees within the prescribed time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must pay the annual fee for the year in which the patent right is granted and the stamp tax as indicated. Time limit: within 2 months from the date of receipt of the Notification to go through formalities of registration; this time limit cannot be extended. Failure to complete formalities or pay fees within the time limit results in entitlement to patent being deemed abandoned and announcement of abandonment. A request for reinstatement may be made within the prescribed time limit when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of layout-designs of integrated circuits — subject matter and submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter includes IC and PCB layout-designs. Submission methods: Hand delivery to the Patent Office, Mailing to the Patent Office, or E-filing at http://vlsi.cnipa.gov.cn. Required documents: request form, drawing(s), drawing catalog, power of attorney (if agent appointed), and four specimens if the layout-design has been put into commercial exploitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving the Notification Concerning Payment of Prescribed fees: registration fee CNY 2000 and stamp tax CNY 5. There is no reduction or postponement and no annual fee for layout-design registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection duration for layout-designs of integrated circuits
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection duration: 10 years starting from the date of filing or from the date of putting it into commercial exploitation, whichever is earlier; regardless of registration or commercial exploitation, it is not protected after 15 years from completion of the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose filing or commercialization date carefully to maximize protection term; note absolute 15-year cutoff from completion of design.
